newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jesus icon said to weep in Bethlehem.
newsitem.headline: Jesus icon said to weep in Bethlehem.

text.p: Pilgrims at Bethlehem's Church of the Nativity say a fourth-century painting of Jesus has begun to weep just above the grotto where tradition holds Christ was born.
"This is a miracle and a sign that Jesus sent us to strengthen our belief," said Father Anastasios, Bethlehem representative of Jerusalem's Greek Orthodox Archbishop Diodoros.
Father Anastasios dismissed criticism the weeping Jesus was a ploy to lure tourists to Bethlehem this Christmas, the second under Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's rule.
"I don't know what this means for tourism, this is a religious matter," Father Anastasios insisted.
Sadika Hamida told Reuters she was the first to see the weeping icon.
"About four weeks ago, a light came from the column and the picture of the messiah Jesus, peace be upon him, began to cry,"

"It was beautiful, beautiful, beautiful. He opened and closed his eye and later tears fell, red tears," she said, pointing to red streaks at the base of the marble column on which the icon is painted.
"I have been coming to this church for 22 years and it is the first time in history I have seen such a sight," she said.
Greek Cypriot pilgrims in the church on Thursday fell to their knees and wept before the painting after saying Jesus had winked at them.
Sceptics dismissed the winking Jesus as an optical trick. They said one of Christ's eyes was brighter than the other, creating an illusion that the dark eye opened and closed.
